newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong economy seen booming under Chinese rule.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong economy seen booming under Chinese rule.

text.p: Hong Kong's economy, which has enjoyed 35 years of uninterrupted growth, will surge ahead when it reverts to Chinese rule in 1997, the British colony's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Monday.

And the Governor of the People's Bank of China, Dai Xianglong, reassured world finance officials that the territory would remain a thriving financial centre after it returns to Beijing rule next July.
Both officials spoke at meetings on the sidelines of the annual International Monetary Fund and World Bank gathering.
"Once people wake up from the excessive pessimism, there will be a real boom in Hong Kong," Tsang said.

He said Hong Kong's recent economic consolidation was a blessing in disguise, considering the struggle for recovery in Europe and economic overheating in the rest of Asia. Inflation has slowed, the property market completely recovered and the stock market is one of the leading performers of 1996.

Tsang dismissed the view that Hong Kong's economic growth would slow as it matures. It was already a post-industrial economy, with more than 80 percent of its output attributable to services, and had the best conditions for staying the course of fast growth and transformation, he said.
China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong told another meeting that China would keep a tight monetary policy to ensure inflation stays below the rate of economic growth.
Dai added that tight monetary policy in mainland China would also benefit Hong Kong, ensuring a smooth financial transition when Hong Kong returns to Chinese governance.
"Those sceptics who have doubted China's commitment to the open door policy no longer can have doubts after witnessing implementation of our economic reforms and its achievements," he said.
As China continues its economic reform, Hong Kong's role as an international financial centre will become increasingly important, the central banker said.
Hong Kong will host next year's IMF/World Bank annual meeting. "(It) will be a magnificent event which commands far-reaching historical significance," Dai said.
